name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
one_liner: A free add-on that trains your AI coding assistant to write the smallest possible fix instead of over-engineering a solution, saving you code review time and hosting cost.
buyer: An engineering manager paying per-token for a team's AI coding usage, who wants smaller diffs and lower cloud spend without policing every pull request personally.
business_use_cases: A startup with a metered AI coding budget installs it to cut token spend and review time, since the agent stops adding unrequested libraries and abstractions.
A code-review-as-a-service business uses it internally so AI-drafted pull requests are small enough for a human reviewer to approve quickly.
A bootcamp teaches it to students as an example of prompting discipline, showing measurable before/after diffs.

money_ideas.idea: Run a paid workshop series on 'minimal-diff AI coding' for engineering teams, using this skill as the demo.
Build a hosted dashboard that tracks an org's AI-generated LOC/cost before and after adopting the skill, sold as a subscription add-on.

steal_this: Take the published benchmark numbers (54% less code, 20% cheaper) and turn them into a one-page cost-savings calculator landing page that captures leads for a paid AI-coding-audit service.
